advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile provenance header_names with actual delivery (record only names that extra_headers_for would attach) or document that it records configured-not-delivered names.
evidence: runner.py:530 `header_names=sorted(cfg.headers),` — passes the whole configured set regardless of base_url or drop
structured_run.py:352 `if not cfg.base_url or not cfg.headers: return None` — nothing is delivered without base_url
headers.py:270-271 `if substituted is None: continue  # an absent substituend drops the header` — dropped headers still appear in cfg.headers
runner.py:512 comment: provenance is meant to 'stamp WHAT actually ran'
advisory.finding: provenance_for records header NAMES from the full configured set (`sorted(cfg.headers)`) unconditionally, but delivery (extra_headers_for) only attaches headers when base_url is set and drops any header whose ${run:...} substituend is absent. A signed verdict can therefore attest header names that were never sent on the wire (no base_url) or were dropped (absent trace/ticket), contradicting the S5/343b principle that provenance stamps WHAT actually ran.
scenarios: Operator configures headers but no base_url: verdict claims header_names that were never attached.
A ${run:trace_id} header configured globally but the op is review-code/standalone (no trace): header is dropped from the wire yet still named in the signed provenance.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the delivery-seam run substitution honors the `$$` escape so an escaped literal ${run:...} is not re-substituted.
evidence: headers.py:109-110 `$$` escapes to a literal `$` so `$${VAR}` yields `${VAR}` unsubstituted
headers.py:236 `_RUN_PLACEHOLDER_RE = re.compile(r"\$\{" + RUN_NAMESPACE + r":([^}]*)\}")` — no `$$` awareness
headers.py:296 `substituted = _RUN_PLACEHOLDER_RE.sub(_one, value)` — runs on the already-de-escaped cfg value, cannot tell an escaped literal from a real placeholder
advisory.finding: An operator-escaped literal placeholder is wrongly re-substituted at the delivery seam. A header value written `$${run:trace_id}` is de-escaped by config-time `substitute` to the literal text `${run:trace_id}` and stored in cfg.headers; `_RUN_PLACEHOLDER_RE` then matches that literal and substitutes the run value, defeating the operator's `$$` escape.
scenarios: Operator intends a literal ${run:trace_id} in a header via $${run:trace_id}; the delivered header instead contains the substituted run value or is dropped as absent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a header value with literal text around a present ${run:...} placeholder (e.g. 'tenant-${run:operation}') resolves to the concatenated 'tenant-review-plan'.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/headers.py: `substituted = _RUN_PLACEHOLDER_RE.sub(_one, value)` — the added _substitute_run does a regex substitution supporting placeholders embedded in literal text
All present-value tests use bare placeholders: `headers={"x-corp-tag": "rebar", "x-trace": "${run:trace_id}"}` and assert `out["extra_headers"] == {..., "x-trace": "a" * 32}`
ABSENCE: no test drives a value like `headers={"x-t": "tenant-${run:operation}"}` and asserts the resolved header is `"tenant-review-plan"`
advisory.finding: The ${run:...} substitution into a header value that also contains surrounding literal text (a partial substitution) is untested; every present-value test asserts on a value that is exactly one bare placeholder (e.g. 'x-trace': '${run:trace_id}'), so a regression in re.sub-based interpolation that mishandled prefix/suffix text would not be caught.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider moving the runner.py module-size-cap assertion into the size-lint tooling rather than a behavior test.
evidence: This reads the source file and asserts on its line count, not on any runtime behavior of the header-delivery change
advisory.finding: test_runner_stays_within_the_module_size_cap asserts a source line-count metric (<= 800) rather than any behavior; it is a linter-owned module-size check expressed as a test and a change-detector that breaks when a behavior-preserving edit (e.g. an added comment) crosses the line count with no observable-behavior change.
